design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing only - end our catering account - and the whole of the
difficulty is what the agent has to discover before that can be answered. The charter says the closing figure "is not
fixed until every order delivered on the agreement carries an invoice entry"; the records show a buffet served on
2026-03-06 with a delivery entry and no invoice entry; nothing anywhere names the invoicing action, so the agent must
read the invoicing policy, see that its write is the one that brings an invoice entry about, bill that order, and only
then work out the closing figure on the world its own write has changed. Neither figure can be looked up: the invoice
is composed of five rules over the order ledger, the agreement's tenure and the client's cafe contract at the delivery
site, and the closing figure is composed of five more over a twelve-month reconciliation of invoices, cancellation
charges, service credits and payments. Getting the order of the two writes wrong is not a procedural slip but an
arithmetic one: the closing figure computed on the opening world is 27618.25 instead of 20943.77.

SCOPE. Already occupied by earlier tasks: nothing, this is task 0 of 2. Claimed here: the two problems
catering_ext_delivered_order_invoicing (tool raise_catering_invoice_cb57dc9d) and catering_ext_agreement_closure_settlement (tool confirm_agreement_closure_1e20ba9d) - the billing of a served order and the settlement an agreement closes
on. Left for task 1: the whole cancellation half of the charter - what the value standing on an order is when the
client pulls it, and what the charge that cancellation carries comes to - with its own two tools. The two tasks share
no policy, no tool, no target write and no source of difficulty: this one is about money owed at the end of a
relationship, task 1 about money owed when work is pulled.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py on this difficulty, --task 0):
  {"task": 0, "key": "env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/catering_order_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}
The tree therefore carries exactly one prerequisite problem, and each of the two computations declares exactly five
factors. The invoicing problem took 5; the closure problem took 5.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  Root problem: catering_ext_agreement_closure_settlement - the closing figure, the thing the caller asks for.
  Prerequisite problem: catering_ext_delivered_order_invoicing - the invoice for the order already served.
  Edge root <- prerequisite: kind value_input, gate invoiced_12m (a compute binding of the root), form state.
    Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the root policy's own rule:
    "The closing figure is not fixed until every order delivered on the agreement carries an invoice entry."
    Four-point test: (1) it joins this policy's own result - the closing figure - to what it waits on with the ordering
    connective "until", in the negated direction, and rewrites exactly into the affirmative "The closing figure is
    fixed only after every order delivered on the agreement carries an invoice entry" with no condition added, dropped
    or split; the direction is the one this desk uses for a figure it will not commit to, as against a charge that "is
    fixed only after" what it rests on. (2) Its waiting side is a record-visible state - an invoice entry standing
    against a delivered order - named in the words the order history itself uses; it names no action and no performer.
    (3) It carries no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id. (4) Its strength is a hard
    requirement ("not ... until") over the closed set of orders that carry a delivery entry, exactly the scope of the
    edge's condition, no wider and no narrower.
    One-write proof for the state form: of the writes this difficulty declares, only the invoicing problem produces an
    entry of the invoice kind on a catering agreement; the closure write produces no ledger entry at all, and task 1's
    two writes produce a cancellation entry and a cancellation charge. A reader who sees that the delivery of
    2026-03-06 carries no invoice entry and reads the invoicing policy's own rule - "The amount invoiced for a catering
    order that has been served is worked out from the value the delivery entry most recently recorded on the agreement
    carries" - has exactly one action open to them, and it is the one gold takes.
    Handling-time condition: every order on the agreement that carries a delivery entry also carries an invoice entry
    standing against the same order reference. Resolving action: raise_catering_invoice_cb57dc9d, owner agent.
    Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: the delivery entry for CO-719044 posted 2026-03-06 stands in
    catering_orders, and no row of catering_orders carries event_type catering_order_invoiced with that order
    reference; the agreement's receivable_balance_usd is 4530.00, which is the invoices and cancellation charges on
    file less payments and credits and contains nothing for CO-719044.
    Topological order: invoicing, then closure. Parallel edges: none - a single edge admits one order.
    Deletion sensitivity (actually run): skipping the invoicing write and replaying everything else gives a closing
    figure of 27618.25 rather than 20943.77.
  Customer's own write: the root problem's target tool confirm_agreement_closure_1e20ba9d is owner=user. Base is explicit that "Only the client
    may end a catering agreement", so the in-person semantics are the charter's own, and the act completes on the spot:
    the agent unlocks and hands it over, the client runs it, and the confirmation with the closing day comes back into
    the shared transcript.
  user_scenario names no prerequisite problem: see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint.
  The tool layer validates nothing: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write subject catering_order_invoiced (the invoicing step). Governing base policies: catering_invoicing_terms and
  catering_combination_cafe_interaction, both of which declare eligibility: [], so neither imposes a gate on an invoice
  entry; each is carried as a policy_scope precondition. No time gate applies to invoicing anywhere in base, so
  temporal_feasibility is empty for this step. Inherited item by item and not overridden: that an order is only
  invoiced once it has been delivered (CO-719044 carries a delivery entry of 2026-03-06, so it is); that an order
  cancelled before delivery is never invoiced as an order (this one was served, not cancelled); that the standing
  discount and the volume discount are added together rather than the better taken (the compute adds 3.00 and 0.75);
  that neither discount is applied to the delivery fee or the rush surcharge (both are added after the discounted food
  and beverage value); that a consolidated invoice never gathers orders from two service levels (this invoice carries
  one order). Overridden, declared clause by clause in the policy's overwrite, four entries: the base sentence fixing
  the composition and the ninety-day window, replaced by this policy's own ordering sentence; the base sentence
  waiving the delivery fee where the cafe kitchen produces the order, replaced by this policy's sentence moving that
  concession onto the service charge; the base sentence holding the ordinary delivery fee whatever the cafe does,
  replaced by the standing-round sentence that can lower it to half or to none; and the base sentence fixing the
  consolidation basis per service level, replaced by this policy's opening sentence, which bills the one served order
  the delivery entry most recently recorded carries. Nothing this policy does to a scored quantity is left silent
  against base.
  Write subject catering_agreement_closed (the closure step). Governing base policy: catering_hold_and_closure_terms,
  gate lifecycle_state, kind state, authority system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key
  catering_agreements.catering_agreement_id bound to the action's catering_agreement_id. Condition: "A hold, a reinstatement or a closure is only worked while the agreement stands active, on credit hold or closed, and never while it is still in credit review, where the application is withdrawn instead."
  At frozen_time the agreement's status is active, one of the three the gate admits, and the agreement the action names
  is the same row the status was read from. Negative boundary: were the status pending_credit_review the gate would
  fail and the correct terminal state would be to withdraw the application rather than close it; were it already
  closed the gate would pass, which is why the gate alone does not decide the figure. No time gate: closure in base
  carries a notice period but no temporal_basis, so temporal_feasibility is empty for this step too; the notice period
  enters only as the early-exit factor's date span, measured from frozen_time to agreement_end_date 2026-08-04
  (145 days), where 90 days (twice the 45 notice days) is the boundary: at 91 days the first tier applies, at
  exactly 90 the second.
  Inherited and not overridden: that only the client may end the agreement (which is why the tool is owner=user); that
  a closed agreement keeps its invoices, credits and history (the closure write deletes nothing); that an agreement is
  not closed while an order stands accepted and unserved (at frozen_time every placed order on the agreement carries
  either a delivery entry or a cancellation entry, so none stands accepted and unserved). Overridden and declared: the
  shortfall sentence and the notice sentence.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
  Invoicing step: the narrowest object is the single catering order CO-719044 under this agreement. The correlation
  key is order_reference, which both its placement entry and its delivery entry carry, and which the invoice entry
  written repeats. Rows that enter its value: only its own delivery entry (the latest delivery entry by posting date,
  posted 2026-03-06, later than every other delivery entry on the agreement). Rows on the same agreement excluded:
  the seven earlier orders, each of which already carries its own invoice entry and a distinct order reference; the two
  cancelled orders CO-707930 and CO-714462, which carry cancellation entries rather than delivery entries. Nothing has
  settled CO-719044: no payment entry quotes an invoice reference for it, because no invoice exists for it yet.
  Closure step: the object is the agreement itself, keyed by catering_agreement_id. The aggregates it reconciles are
  scoped by the twelve months ending on the closing day and by event type; the existing service credits are correlated
  to the orders they answer through the invoice references INV-CT-338920 and INV-CT-343506, and the existing
  cancellation charges to their own cancellation entries through order references CO-707930 and CO-714462 on the same
  notice days, so neither is double-counted against another order.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
  The seven served-and-billed orders (placement, delivery and invoice entries each) carry the invoiced spend and the
  invoiced order count behind the volume step and the counted spend, and the delivery counts behind the rush tier and
  the delivery-charge tier. Remove the entries of 2025-04-18 to 2025-08-15 and the twelve-month invoiced spend falls
  below five thousand dollars, so the volume step becomes none (9980.00 less 1620.00, 1340.00 and 2050.00 leaves
  4970.00). The delivery charge is held off by a wider margin, and the counterfactual was re-run rather than assumed:
  the twelve months carry eight deliveries against a standing-round threshold of five, so removing three still leaves
  five and the charge is still none and the invoice still 6167.65; removing four leaves four, which is the
  two-or-more tier, and the charge becomes the half fee of 27.50 with the invoice at 6195.15; only removing seven
  leaves one, below both thresholds, and the charge returns at the whole 55.00 with the invoice at 6750.05. Their
  dates are deliberately spread so that the three-month window the computation document uses picks up only the last
  two - the near-miss a careless reader takes for the whole year.
  The two cancelled orders and their charges of 1450.00 and 980.00 put the agreement on the first tier of the
  counted-spend method; remove them and the method falls to its baseline and the shortfall rises.
  The two service credits of 310.00 and 425.00 are what separates the first tier of that method from the second.
  The five payments fix both the unsettled balance of 4530.00 and the date of the most recent payment entry,
  2025-12-30, 72 days before the closing day; move that payment inside sixty days and the late charge falls from
  twice the monthly percentage to once, and inside thirty days to nothing.
  The order served on 2026-03-06 and not billed is the prerequisite itself.
  The Full Service Cafe contract at CS-244 is the cross-difficulty evidence, read twice: once for the service charge
  concession and once for the minimum tested against. Remove it and both fall to their baselines.
  Automatic clauses checked: base's credit-exposure clause puts an agreement on hold when open orders reach the
  open-order multiple of the credit limit - at frozen_time no order on the agreement stands accepted and unserved, so
  open-order exposure is nil against an 18000.00 limit and no hold is owed. Base's late-charge clause is a quotation
  raised when a bill is chased rather than a standing debt, and is not lit by the seed. No cache field exists on a
  catering agreement other than receivable_balance_usd, which is seeded exactly equal to the ledger sum, so this task
  designs no cache trap and check_cache_diff has nothing to report.

PERSONA. Marla Fenwick is written brisk and slightly apologetic, an operations manager doing the tidy part of a
decision made above her. What she volunteers at the opening: the company, that she wants the catering agreement
closed, that she wants it done today on the call, and that she is authorised to close it. What she gives only when
asked: the direct line 3125470188, then the client account code CA-22417, and an explicit refusal to dig for the
postcode or the email unless they are really needed - a definite branch rather than an improvisation. What she reacts
to, and only after the agent has said it: an explanation that something has to be written up first (she says to go
ahead and waits), a figure read to her (she asks for it to be put on the account and nothing more), and the closing
action handed over (she asks for the exact wording and figure, repeats them once, runs it, and closes the call on the
confirmation). She never states an amount, never names an order, and if asked what is outstanding says she does not
know and refers the desk to the record. Her last reaction answers the last gold action and asks for nothing beyond it.

DIFFICULTY IN DEPTH AND BREADTH. Depth: surface goal (close the account) -> the closure policy's own prerequisite
sentence -> the records show a delivered order with no invoice entry -> the invoicing policy is the only one whose
write produces an invoice entry -> the invoice must itself be computed from five rules -> only then is the closing
figure computable, on the world that write produced. Breadth: at the closing step alone the answer depends in parallel
on the agreement's tenure, on the client's cafe contract in another difficulty's product, on three separate
twelve-month aggregates over different event types, on the count of invoiced orders, on the date of the most recent
payment, on the unsettled balance and on the days left to run on the term.

EASY MISTAKES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Counting the trailing spend over three months because that is the
window the computation document states, and missing that a two-year-old agreement counts twelve: the tenure is on the
agreement row. Charging the service charge because the computation document says to: the cafe contract at the delivery
site is what removes it. Charging the delivery fee: the delivery count and the site on the delivery entry remove it.
Working the closing figure on the opening ledger: the prerequisite sentence forbids it and the figure moves by 6674.48.
Taking the whole shortfall: the spend counted reaches half the minimum tested against and the agreement carried enough
invoiced orders, so only half falls due. Testing against the full 42000.00: the cafe contract and the two years in
force reduce it to 31500.00.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by the company name; verify on the telephone number and the client account code;
read the agreement (Attended Buffet Account, active, standing discount 3.00, delivery site CS-244, unsettled 4530.00,
term to 2026-08-04); read the whole order history; read the cafe contract at CS-244. See that CO-719044 was delivered
on 2026-03-06 and carries no invoice entry, and that the closing figure waits on that. Compute the invoice (6167.65) and
raise it. Recompute on the new world: minimum tested against 31500.00, spend counted 17842.65, shortfall 13657.35,
half due 6828.68, late charge 267.44, early-exit charge 3150.00, unsettled 10697.65, closing figure 20943.77. Unlock
the closing action, hand it to the client with the figure, and let her run it.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. Both computations were evaluated with the gate's own evaluator
(skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py, build_env and eval_compute) on the handling-time world of each
step - the invoice on the opening ledger, the closing figure on the ledger after the invoice write had been replayed
with the real tools. Outputs: invoice result 6167.65 over 21 bindings and 13 branches, reconciling 25 history rows;
closing figure 20943.77 over 22 bindings and 14 branches, reconciling 17 history rows. Per-factor baseline
substitution on the invoice gave 6211.60, 6211.60, 6957.28, 5640.25 and 6222.65; every factor at baseline at once gave 6534.99. On
the closing figure it gave 39322.44, 21791.27, 27772.44, 20676.33 and 17793.77; all at once gave 36550.00. Prerequisite sensitivity:
skipping the invoice write gave 27618.25. Every one of those figures differs from the gold it belongs to, and each is
recorded in computations[] where the gate recomputes it.

RULE AND COMPUTE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Forward: compute_basis quotes a rule sentence verbatim for every binding that reads
the world or makes a choice - the delivery-entry read, the tenure span, the windowed spend, the invoiced order count,
the volume ladder, the total rate, the discounting, the two cafe reads, the concession ladder, the service charge, the
placement and service dates, the lead hours, the delivery counts, the rush ladder and its base, the site read, the
delivery ladder, and the final ordering; and on the closing policy for the tenure, the two cafe reads, the benchmark
ladder, the three windowed sums, the two counts, the counted-spend method, the shortfall, the invoiced order count,
the share ladder, the unsettled read, the last payment date, the day span, the late ladder, the ceiling, the term span,
the early-exit ladder and the final ordering. Reverse: every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a
binding. The sensitive words were cross-checked - "the twelve months ending on the day the invoice is raised" against
within_months=12, "three months" against within_months=3, "held to the late charge ceiling" against MN, "never less
than nothing" against MX, "rounded to two decimal places only at the end" against the single RND on result. The
semantics that could be read two ways are pinned in prose: the discount acts once on the served value and not again
("the discount does not act a second time on any later step"), the service charge acts on the discounted food and
beverage value and never on the rush surcharge or the delivery charge, the rush surcharge acts on the value the
delivery entry carries rather than on the discounted value, the ceiling on the late charge applies after the
percentage has been taken, and the closing figure adds its four parts in a stated order and rounds once at the end.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. The invoicing step carries both governing base policies as policy_scope
preconditions with pre-action seed evidence, and its stage fact - that the catering was served and confirmed on
2026-03-06 - cites the official delivery entry rather than the persona. The closure step carries the lifecycle_state
gate with the agreement's own status and reference as pre-action system evidence, correlated to the action's
catering_agreement_id, and its stage fact cites the preceding step rather than asserting it. Every required customer
input is quoted verbatim from user_scenario. Nothing in either step waits on an event outside this conversation: the
delivery had already happened before the call, and both writes land synchronously under one frozen_time.

BLIND RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this rationale
masked, and working only from what the published catering rules will say, the tool schemas, the rows the finders
return and Marla's actual lines: the caller wants the agreement ended; the closure rule says the closing figure is not
fixed until every delivered order carries an invoice entry; the order history shows CO-719044 delivered 2026-03-06
with no invoice entry; the invoicing rule is the only one that books an invoice, and it prices from the delivery entry
most recently recorded, giving 6167.65 once the twelve-month window, the volume step, the cafe concession, the rush
half-rate and the standing round are applied; with that entry written the closing rule yields 20943.77. The blind pass
agrees with gold on the act, the order, the two figures and their order; no second reading of the visible text reaches
a different write sequence, because the prerequisite sentence forbids fixing the figure first and the ledger shows
exactly one delivered order without an invoice.

REVISIONS.
Round 1: none - the world was laid out to the factor design rather than the other way round, and the first
handling-time evaluation of both computations matched the figures the design intended.
Round 2, closing the source-layer audit (T0-F1, and the charter-global F-3 and O-1 that touch this task's policies).
  T0-F1. Symptom: the seed-row paragraph asserted "remove three of the deliveries and the delivery charge returns at
  55.00". Root cause: the counterfactual was written against the wrong tier boundary - the standing-round tier needs
  five deliveries, not eight, so removing three still satisfies it. Change: the sentence was re-run rather than
  re-argued, and now records what the recomputation gives - eight deliveries in the window, removing three leaves five
  and the charge is still none with the invoice still 6167.65; removing four leaves four, the two-or-more tier, the
  half fee of 27.50 and an invoice of 6195.15; only removing seven leaves one, below both thresholds, the whole 55.00
  and an invoice of 6750.05. The relationship the sentence was there to support - that the delivery record is
  load-bearing - still holds, and is now stated truthfully. No scored value moved: the invoice is 6167.65 and the
  closing figure 20943.77 as before.
  F-3 (charter-global, no cost to this task's world but a silent divergence). Symptom: base's "Where that cafe contract
  does not permit catering out of its kitchen, the order is produced at the district kitchen and the ordinary delivery
  fee applies however close the cafe is" was inherited while this policy's standing-round factor can set the delivery
  charge to none or to half. Change: declared as a third overwrite entry, quoting that base sentence and replacing it
  with the standing-round sentence of this policy's own rule. Base itself is untouched.
  O-1 (charter-global). Symptom: base's consolidation sentence was neither followed nor declared, while this policy
  bills one served order per call. Change: declared as a fourth overwrite entry, replaced by this policy's opening
  sentence. No scored value moved.
  Observations left standing, with reasons: T0-O1 (the closing computation's near-miss is by event family rather than
  by window - two catering_order_cancelled rows carry charge_code cancellation_fee exactly as the charge rows do, and a
  reader filtering by charge_code adds 4860.00 of phantom charges; the invoicing computation on the same task carries
  the window near-miss); T0-O2 (the LATEST-scoped identification of the order to invoice coincides with the only
  delivered-and-uninvoiced order on this world, and narrowing it would change the policy rather than the task);
  O-4 (base's "the desk records the request" has no tool in this difficulty and cannot produce a competing write).
  Gate block re-run after the changes: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK,
  GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
Round 3. The round-2 re-audit closed this task on all four relationships and raised no finding against it; its one red
light, R2-F1, lands on the cancellation registration policy, which this task does not claim. One change nevertheless
reaches this task's two policies and is recorded here so that nothing is assumed untouched: the join key each
cross-category read uses is now declared alongside the fields it returns, so cross_category.reads on both policies
lists site_code with status and variant_name. That field is the one the cafe contract is matched on
(CFIELD('cafe','status', site_code=F('delivery_site_code')) and the CPARAM beside it), and db_schema.json declares both
catering_agreements.delivery_site_code and cafe_contracts.site_code as "CS- followed by 3 digits", so the join is
inside one namespace and neither record is bent to make it hold. `reads` is a declaration of what the policy looks at,
read by no compute and by no gate, so no scored quantity could move. It was re-derived rather than assumed: the
invoice recomputes to 6167.65 and the closing figure to 20943.77, the edge-skip figure to 27618.25, the two
whole-baseline fall-backs to 6534.99 and 36550.00, and all ten factor substitutions to the same figures this task
recorded in round 2. The mechanical face sweep run for round 3 covered these two policies as well: every ladder tier
condition and every prose outcome uses only words its policy's rule states, and the cafe join is stated identically in
the rule, the compute and the ladders.
  Gate block re-run after the round-3 change: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK,
  COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
Round 4. The render-layer audit matched this task on every scored parameter, every tier, both fall-back numbers, the
problem tree, the edge form and the tool sequence, and raised no finding against it. Its red light, C1, is the
cross-product vocabulary of task 1's banquet read. A change nevertheless reaches this task's two policies, for the same
hazard on their cafe read, and it was made deliberately rather than by copying: both policies said the cafe contract
"stands open" and that its service model "takes catering out of that kitchen". Neither phrase belongs to the product
whose records they point at. The Workplace Cafe Management Program corpus says "stands active" of that state and
contrasts it with suspended, in transition out, mobilizing, proposed and closed; "open" is undefined there, and the
catering base rule it refines is explicit that a cafe standing suspended stops catering out of that kitchen, so a
reader taking "open" as "not closed" would have admitted a suspended cafe the compute (cafe_status == 'active')
excludes. The cafe corpus also prints the parameter as whether catering may be ordered out of the cafe kitchen. Both
conditions now read "stands active" and "permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen", in the words the other
product publishes and the words the compute binds. Every face moved together - rule, baseline.rule, compute_basis, the
cross_category note and each ladder tier condition - and a mechanical scan reports zero occurrences of the retired
phrasing anywhere in the charter.
Nothing about this task was assumed untouched. Every figure was re-derived on the rebuilt charter: the invoice
recomputes to 6167.65 and the closing figure to 20943.77, the edge-skip figure to 27618.25, the two whole-baseline
fall-backs to 6534.99 and 36550.00, and all ten factor substitutions to 6211.60, 6211.60, 6957.28, 5640.25, 6222.65,
39322.44, 21791.27, 27772.44, 20676.33 and 17793.77 - every one identical to the figures both audits verified. The
tier each factor takes is unchanged: the seeded cafe contract at CS-244 stands active and its Full Service Cafe model
permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen, which is the same tier under either wording, so the change is a
change of words only and the scored values could not move. The identifier band is unchanged and re-checked.

re-run will be recorded here if a later gate turns anything red.
user_scenario:
Marla Fenwick runs workplace operations for Greyfriar Analytics Group out of their River North office, and she has been the one who signs off catering for the client floor for the better part of three years. The firm has decided to bring hospitality in-house from the summer, and her job this morning is the tidy part of that decision: she wants the corporate catering account ended, properly, with whatever it closes on put onto a final bill she can hand to finance. She is brisk, a little apologetic about it, and completely uninterested in being talked out of it.

She opens by saying she is calling from Greyfriar Analytics Group and that she wants to close the catering agreement. If she is asked to confirm who she is, she reads out the direct line on the account, 3125470188, and if a second detail is wanted she reads the client account code off the last invoice, CA-22417. She has the billing postcode and the invoicing email somewhere but says she would rather not dig for them unless they are really needed, and if pressed she simply repeats the two she has already given. She does not know any internal reference numbers and says so if she is asked for one, telling the agent that whatever is on their screen is what the firm has.

Asked when she wants it to end, she says today, as of this call. She does not want a figure to take away and think about; she wants the account ended while she is on the phone, and she is content for the desk to work out what it closes on. She is clear that she is authorised to end the agreement for the firm, saying the decision was made upstairs and she is the one who signs. If the agent explains that something on the account has to be written up before the account can be ended, she tells them to go ahead and do it, says she is not going to argue about paperwork, and stays on the line.

If the agent gives her a figure the account will close on, she does not measure it against anything of her own; she says finance will want it on a statement and asks for it to be put on the account, and nothing further. If she is handed the closing action to run herself, she asks for the exact wording and the exact figure, repeats them back once and runs it; once it comes back confirmed she says that is all she needed and thanks the agent. She never volunteers an amount of her own, and if she is asked what she thinks is outstanding she says she genuinely does not know, that finance handles the invoices, and asks the agent to read it off the record.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the client organisation profile from the company name the caller states, and read its contact details, site, billing postcode and opening date.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the profile there is no client to attach the agreement lookup to, and no record to check the caller's stated details against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller matched the direct line and the client account code held on the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing may be quoted back about the catering account, and no money may be moved on it, until the caller has passed verification in this session.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's catering service agreement: its service level, state, term dates, default delivery site, standing discount and unsettled balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The service level fixes the minimum annual catering spend, the service charge, the delivery fee, the rush percentage, the notice days, the monthly late percentage and its ceiling; the term dates and the standing discount enter both computations directly.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole order history on the agreement: placements, deliveries, invoices, cancellations, cancellation charges, service credits and payments, with their dates and amounts.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every history aggregate rests on these rows - the delivery entry the invoice is worked out from, the invoiced spend and order count behind the volume step and the counted spend, the delivery counts behind the rush and delivery-charge tiers, the cancellation charges and service credits the counted-spend method folds in, and the most recent payment entry behind the late charge; they are also where a reader sees that the order served on 2026-03-06 carries no invoice entry.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's workplace cafe management contract at the delivery site: which service model it holds and whether it stands active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The service charge concession tier and the tier of the minimum tested against are both decided from whether that cafe contract stands active and whether its service model permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden catering invoicing action so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the invoice for the catering order served on 2026-03-06, writing an invoice entry against order CO-719044 and lifting the agreement's unsettled catering balance by the amount billed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only catering_ext_delivered_order_invoicing produces invoice_amount_usd; the invoice entry it writes is also what the closing figure waits on.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.catering_agreement_id: The internal reference of the one corporate catering service agreement returned for this client by the agreement lookup at step 2. Basis: the agreement lookup's own contract - "Retrieve the corporate catering service agreements on file" - returns the agreement row with its reference; the caller states no reference at all ("She does not know any internal reference numbers and says so if she is asked for one"). Uniqueness: the lookup returns exactly one catering agreement for this client, so any agent who follows the caller's company through the profile lookup lands on the same reference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The internal reference of the client organisation profile returned by the profile lookup at step 0 for the company the caller names. Basis: the profile lookup returns "A single matching profile" in full for the stated organisation name. Uniqueness: exactly one profile carries the organisation name the caller states, and the agreement read at step 2 carries the same client reference, so the two agree.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.order_reference: CO-719044. Basis: the order history read at step 3 carries a delivery entry with that order reference posted on 2026-03-06, and the invoicing rule states that the amount invoiced "is worked out from the value the delivery entry most recently recorded on the agreement carries". Uniqueness: that is the only order on the agreement carrying a delivery entry and no invoice entry; every other delivered order already carries one, so no other reference can be the order now owed an invoice.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_date: 2026-03-06. Basis: the delivery entry for CO-719044 in the order history records the service day as 2026-03-06, and the invoicing tool asks for "the day the catering was served". Uniqueness: the order's own placement and delivery entries both carry that service day, and no other day is recorded against that order reference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_amount_usd: 6167.65. The value the delivery entry most recently recorded on the agreement carries is 5860.00. The agreement has been in force 25 months on 2026-03-12, two years or more, so the catering spend is counted over the twelve months ending that day: the seven invoice entries of 2025-04-18, 2025-06-27, 2025-08-15, 2025-10-09, 2025-12-04, 2026-01-23 and 2026-02-13 sum to 9980.00, and the same twelve months carry 7 invoiced orders. That spend reaches five thousand dollars with two or more invoiced orders but not fifteen thousand, so the volume step earned is 0.75 of a point; with the standing discount of 3.00 recorded on the agreement the total discount rate is 3.75, and the value is reduced once by it to 5640.25. The client holds a Full Service Cafe contract at CS-244 that stands active and whose service model permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen, so no service charge is raised. The order was accepted on 2026-03-04 for service at 11:30 on 2026-03-06, 48 hours ahead of service and so inside the 72-hour standard lead time for the service level, and the agreement carried 5 deliveries in the six months ending 2026-03-12, three or more, so half the 18.00 rush percentage applies: 9.0 on the value the delivery entry carries, 527.40. The agreement carried 8 deliveries in the twelve months ending that day, five or more, all to CS-244, the site named on the agreement, so no delivery charge is raised. 5640.25 plus 0.00 plus 527.40 plus 0.00 gives 6167.65.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Hand the closing action to the client, since only the client may end their own catering agreement.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair for a customer-owned action; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The client ends the catering agreement herself: it moves to closed, the closing day is stamped on it, and the figure it closes on is set as the amount left to settle.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only catering_ext_agreement_closure_settlement produces closing_settlement_usd, and only the client may end the agreement.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.catering_agreement_id: The internal reference of the client's one corporate catering service agreement, read from the agreement lookup at step 2 and given to the client by the agent when the closing action is handed over. Basis: the closing action asks for "the reference number of the corporate catering service agreement the client is ending, as the desk reads it off the client's agreement record"; the caller has none of her own ("She does not know any internal reference numbers and says so if she is asked for one"). Uniqueness: the client holds exactly one catering agreement, so only one reference can be passed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.closing_settlement_usd: 20943.77. The agreement has run 25 months and the client holds a cafe contract at CS-244 that stands active and whose service model permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen, so the minimum tested against is three quarters of the 42000.00 minimum annual catering spend printed against the Attended Buffet Account, 31500.00. The twelve months ending 2026-03-12 carry invoice entries totalling 16147.65 - the seven already on file plus the invoice raised at the preceding step for CO-719044 - together with 2430.00 of cancellation charges raised on 2025-09-12 and 2026-01-08 and 735.00 of service credits allowed on 2025-09-05 and 2025-11-05; cancellation charges and service credits both stand in that window, so the spend counted is 16147.65 plus 2430.00 less 735.00, that is 17842.65. The shortfall is 31500.00 less 17842.65, 13657.35. The spend counted reaches half of the minimum tested against but not three quarters of it, and the agreement carried 8 invoiced orders in those twelve months, so half the shortfall falls due: 6828.68. The most recent payment entry on the agreement fell on 2025-12-30, 72 days before the closing day and so more than sixty, and an amount stands unsettled, so the late charge is twice the 1.25 monthly late percentage on the 10697.65 standing unsettled, 267.44, well under the 1400.00 ceiling. The agreement is ended with 145 days still to run to 2026-08-04, more than twice the 45 notice days, and the spend counted has not reached three quarters of the minimum tested against, so the early-exit charge is a tenth of that minimum, 3150.00. 6828.68 plus 267.44 plus 3150.00 plus the 10697.65 standing unsettled gives 20943.77.

edges.condition: every order on the agreement that carries a delivery entry also carries an invoice entry standing against the same order reference
edges.policy_source: The closing figure is not fixed until every order delivered on the agreement carries an invoice entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-03-12 the agreement carries a delivery entry for CO-719044 posted on 2026-03-06 and no invoice entry anywhere in its history quoting that order reference; every other delivered order on the agreement carries one, so the condition fails on this one order alone.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Raising the invoice writes an invoice entry for 6167.65 against CO-719044 and lifts the agreement's unsettled balance to 10697.65; the invoiced total inside the twelve-month window rises from 9980.00 to 16147.65, so the condition then holds for every delivered order.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has one edge and therefore one topological order, so no two orders are available to compare: the invoice entry must stand before the closing figure is fixed. The closing figure reads the invoiced total in the twelve-month window, the invoiced order count in that window and the agreement's unsettled balance, all three of which the invoicing write moves, so the reverse order is not merely unordered but arithmetically different.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying with the invoicing write skipped and everything else unchanged, the closing figure computes to 27618.25 instead of 20943.77: the invoiced total in the window falls from 16147.65 to 9980.00, the spend counted falls from 17842.65 to 11675.00, the share of the shortfall that falls due rises from half to the whole of it, and the amount standing unsettled falls from 10697.65 to 4530.00, which also lowers the late charge.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions an order, an invoice, a delivery or a bill that has to be raised first. Marla says only that she wants the catering agreement closed today, that she is authorised to close it, and that she does not know what is outstanding and would rather the desk read it off the record. Her one contribution on the subject is passive and conditional - if the agent explains that something on the account has to be written up before the account can be ended, she tells them to go ahead and stays on the line - and it fires only after the agent has said so. Nothing in the persona names the invoicing problem, the delivered order CO-719044, or any suggestion that something might be outstanding.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_agreement_closure_1e20ba9d in task_tools.py performs one ctx.update on the agreement, setting status, closed_date and receivable_balance_usd from the figure it is given; it reads no order history, makes no test of whether any delivered order is still unbilled, and returns its confirmation whatever the state of the ledger. Called on the opening world it would still write, and would simply write the wrong figure. Likewise raise_catering_invoice_cb57dc9d writes its invoice entry without asking whether the order was delivered or whether an invoice already stands against it.

factor_trace: volume_step_earned (parameter): the seven invoice entries inside the counting window sum to 9980.00 and the twelve months ending 2026-03-12 carry 7 invoiced orders, which reaches five thousand dollars with two or more invoiced orders but not fifteen thousand, so the third tier applies and the volume step earned is 0.75 of a point; the baseline earns no volume step, which would have given 6211.60.

spend_counting_window (method): the agreement began on 2024-02-05 and has been in force 25 months at 2026-03-12, two years or more, so the first tier applies and the catering spend is counted over the twelve months ending that day, giving 9980.00 from the invoice entries of 2025-04-18 through 2026-02-13; the baseline counts it over the three months ending that day, which picks up only the entries of 2026-01-23 and 2026-02-13 and would have given 6211.60.

kitchen_service_concession (parameter, cross-difficulty): the client's Full Service Cafe contract at CS-244 stands active and that service model permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen, so the first tier applies and no service charge is raised; the baseline raises the 14.00 per cent printed against the Attended Buffet Account, which would have given 6957.28.

rush_percentage_carried (parameter): the order was accepted on 2026-03-04 for service at 11:30 on 2026-03-06, 48 hours ahead and so inside the 72-hour standard lead time, and the agreement carried 5 deliveries in the six months ending 2026-03-12, three or more, so the first tier applies and half the 18.00 rush percentage is carried, 9.0, yielding 527.40 on the value the delivery entry carries; the baseline carries no rush percentage, which would have given 5640.25.

standing_round_delivery_charge (parameter): the agreement carried 8 deliveries in the twelve months ending 2026-03-12, five or more, and the delivery entry names CS-244, the site written on the agreement, so the first tier applies and no delivery charge is raised; the baseline raises the 55.00 fee printed against the service level, which would have given 6222.65.

Bindings outside every factor: served_value reads 5860.00 from the delivery entry most recently recorded on the agreement; total_discount_pct adds the 3.00 standing discount on the agreement to the volume step, giving 3.75; discounted_food reduces the served value once by that rate to 5640.25; service_charge and rush_amount apply the two selected percentages to their stated bases; result adds the discounted food and beverage value, the service charge, the rush surcharge and the delivery charge in that order and rounds once at the end.

factor_trace: programme_spend_benchmark (parameter, cross-difficulty): the agreement has run 25 months and the client's Full Service Cafe contract at CS-244 stands active with a service model that permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen, so the first tier applies and the minimum tested against is three quarters of the 42000.00 printed against the Attended Buffet Account, 31500.00; the baseline tests against the whole 42000.00, which would have given 39322.44.

counted_spend_basis (method): the twelve months ending 2026-03-12 carry 2 cancellation charges totalling 2430.00 and 2 service credits totalling 735.00, so the first tier applies and the spend counted is the 16147.65 invoiced plus those charges less those credits, 17842.65; the baseline counts what has been invoiced alone, which would have given 21791.27.

shortfall_share_due (parameter): the spend counted 17842.65 reaches half of the 31500.00 tested against but not three quarters of it, and the agreement carried 8 invoiced orders in those twelve months, so the second tier applies and half the shortfall falls due, 6828.68 of 13657.35; the baseline has the whole shortfall fall due, which would have given 27772.44.

closing_late_charge_rate (parameter): the most recent payment entry on the agreement fell on 2025-12-30, 72 days before the closing day and so more than sixty, and 10697.65 stands unsettled, so the first tier applies and twice the 1.25 monthly late percentage is taken, 2.5, giving 267.44 under the 1400.00 ceiling; the baseline raises no late charge, which would have given 20676.33.

early_exit_charge_share (parameter): the agreement is ended with 145 days still to run to 2026-08-04, more than twice the 45 notice days printed against the service level, and the spend counted has not reached three quarters of the minimum tested against, so the first tier applies and the early-exit charge is a tenth of that minimum, 3150.00; the baseline raises no early-exit charge, which would have given 17793.77.

Bindings outside every factor: shortfall_base is the minimum tested against less the spend counted, floored at nothing, 13657.35; shortfall_due applies the selected share to it; unsettled reads 10697.65 from the agreement after the invoice raised at the preceding step; late_charge applies the selected percentage to that unsettled amount and holds it to the ceiling printed against the service level; result adds the shortfall due, the late charge, the early-exit charge and the unsettled amount in that order and rounds once at the end.
